title: Factors, primes and powers
ks3: Number: factors, multiples, primes, HCF, LCM, powers and roots
intro: Factors, multiples and prime numbers, prime factor trees, HCF and LCM, and squares, cubes and their roots.
description: Free KS3 Maths questions with answers on factors, multiples, prime numbers, prime factorisation, HCF and LCM, squares, cubes and roots. Marked instantly, for ages 9 to 14.

questions.q: Which of these is a factor of 18?
questions.hint: A factor divides into 18 exactly, with nothing left over.
questions.explain: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 exactly, so 6 is a factor. 4 and 8 leave a remainder, and 36 is a multiple of 18, not a factor.

questions.hint: List them in pairs that multiply to 12: 1 × 12, 2 × …
questions.explain: The factor pairs are 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12: that is 6 factors.

questions.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 36?
questions.hint: List the factors of each number and find the biggest one in both lists.
questions.explain: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The biggest in both is 12.

questions.q: Ali puts 24 apples and 40 oranges into identical fruit bags, with nothing left over. What is the largest number of bags that can be made?
questions.hint: The number of bags must divide both 24 and 40. You want the biggest such number.
questions.explain: This is the HCF of 24 and 40. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. The HCF is 8, so 8 bags, each with 3 apples and 5 oranges.

questions.q: Which number is a multiple of 7?
questions.explain: 6 × 7 = 42. The others are not in the 7 times table (57 = 3 × 19).

questions.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
questions.hint: Write out the multiples of each and find the first one in both lists.
questions.explain: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, … Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, … The first in both lists is 12.

questions.q: One bus leaves every 12 minutes and another leaves every 18 minutes. They both leave at 9:00. How many minutes later do they next leave together?
questions.hint: You need the lowest common multiple of 12 and 18.
questions.explain: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, … Multiples of 18: 18, 36, … The LCM is 36, so they leave together again after 36 minutes, at 9:36.

questions.q: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.hint: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
questions.explain: 29 can only be divided by 1 and 29. The others are not prime: 21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3 × 9 and 39 = 3 × 13.

questions.q: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
questions.hint: Check each number from 11 to 19. Even numbers (except 2) are never prime.
questions.explain: The primes between 10 and 20 are 11, 13, 17 and 19. That is 4. (15 = 3 × 5, so it is not prime.)

options: No, because a prime has exactly two factors and 1 has only one
Yes, because it only divides by 1 and itself
No, because it is too small to be a number
questions.hint: Think about how many factors a prime number must have.
questions.explain: A prime number has exactly two different factors. 1 has only one factor (itself), so 1 is not prime. The smallest prime is 2.

questions.q: Which shows 60 written as a product of prime factors?
questions.hint: Every number in the answer must be prime, and they must multiply to 60.
questions.explain: 60 = 2 × 30 = 2 × 2 × 15 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 2² × 3 × 5. The others use 10, 4 or 15, which are not prime, or multiply to 90.

questions.q: What is the square root of 81?
questions.explain: 9 × 9 = 81, so the square root of 81 is 9.

questions.q: What is the cube root of 125?
questions.hint: Which number times itself times itself makes 125?
questions.explain: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so the cube root of 125 is 5.
There are 3 + 4 = 7 fives multiplied together, so 5³ × 5⁴ = 5⁷. When you multiply powers of the same number, add the powers.
